message.content:
I need to find which function or method declared under /bench/home/work/internal/ has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) across the entire repository at /bench/home/work.

Steps:
1. First, list all exported functions/methods declared in Go files under /bench/home/work/internal/ (use grep for `^func` patterns). Collect the function/method names.
2. For each function name found, count how many times it's called across the entire codebase (grep -r for the function name in all .go files, excluding the declaration itself and test files if needed — but actually count ALL callers including tests).
3. Report the top 10 functions by call count, with their declaration file path and approximate fan-in count.

Focus on exported functions (capitalized names) as they're more likely to have high fan-in. Also check unexported ones though.

Be thorough — check ALL functions declared in internal/, not just a sample. The repo is at /bench/home/work.

content.text: 77 Go files and 413 function declarations. Let me extract all function names and then count their usage across the entire codebase. I'll do this systematically.

input.command:
# Extract all function/method declarations with their names and file paths
# For regular functions: func FuncName(
# For methods: func (receiver) MethodName(
grep -rn '^func ' /bench/home/work/internal/ --include='*.go' | sed -E 's/^([^:]+):([0-9]+):func \(([^)]*)\) ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\(.*/\1:\2:method:\4/' | sed -E '/method/!s/^([^:]+):([0-9]+):func ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\(.*/\1:\2:func:\3/' | head -30

# Extract ALL function/method names with their declaration files
# Output format: file:line:name
grep -rn '^func ' /bench/home/work/internal/ --include='*.go' | sed -E 's/^([^:]+):([0-9]+):func \([^)]*\) ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\(.*/\1:\2:\3/' | sed -E '/^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[A-Za-z]/!s/^([^:]+):([0-9]+):func ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\(.*/\1:\2:\3/' | grep -E '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$' > /tmp/all_internal_funcs.txt
wc -l /tmp/all_internal_funcs.txt

input.command:
# Now for each unique function name, count occurrences across the entire repo's .go files
# Exclude the declaration line itself by looking for the name followed by ( but not preceded by "func "
# We'll count all occurrences of "FuncName(" in .go files across the entire repo

# First, let's do this efficiently with a script
while IFS= read -r fname; do
  # Count all occurrences of the function name being called (name followed by open paren)
  # We grep for the pattern and exclude lines that are the func declaration
  count=$(grep -rn "\b${fname}\b" /bench/home/work/ --include='*.go' 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v "^Binary" | \
    grep -cv "^[^:]*:[0-9]*:func " 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "$count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "$count $fname"
  fi
done < /tmp/unique_func_names.txt | sort -rn > /tmp/func_counts.txt

head -50 /tmp/func_counts.txt
input.description: Count all function name references across the codebase

content.text: Now I need to be more precise. For generic names like `Error`, `New`, `Len`, `Format`, `Kind`, etc., the grep counts include calls to completely unrelated functions from other packages. Let me do a more targeted analysis, especially for functions with distinctive names that are unique to `internal/`.

input.command:
# Now let's do a smarter fan-in count:
# For exported functions (capitalized), search for both:
#   - packagename.FuncName  (direct package calls)
#   - .FuncName(            (method calls)
# For unexported functions, they can only be called within the same package,
# so count occurrences within that package directory, excluding the declaration

# Let's filter out test functions (TestXxx, BenchmarkXxx, ExampleXxx) and init() 
# as they aren't called by other code
grep -v -E ':(Test[A-Z]|Benchmark[A-Z]|Example[A-Z_]|init):' /tmp/funcs_with_pkg.txt > /tmp/funcs_nontests.txt
wc -l /tmp/funcs_nontests.txt
input.description: Filter out test and init functions

input.command:
# Hmm, that didn't filter enough. Let me check what test functions look like
grep -E ':(Test[A-Z]|Benchmark[A-Z]|Example)' /tmp/funcs_with_pkg.txt | wc -l

# Filter out Test/Benchmark/Example/init functions properly
grep -v -E ':(Test[A-Z]|Benchmark[A-Z]|Example_|Example[A-Z]|init):' /tmp/funcs_with_pkg.txt > /tmp/funcs_nontests.txt
wc -l /tmp/funcs_nontests.txt
echo "---"
# Also filter: functions from test files that are helpers (like Error, Info in test mocks)
grep -v '_test\.go' /tmp/funcs_nontests.txt > /tmp/funcs_production.txt
wc -l /tmp/funcs_production.txt

# Let me check the init filter
grep ':init:' /tmp/funcs_with_pkg.txt

# Good. Now let's do the smart fan-in count. For all 269 production functions:
# Strategy:
# - For exported funcs (uppercase first letter): count "pkgname.FuncName" across the codebase
#   PLUS count ".FuncName(" for method calls (when it's a method on a type)
# - For unexported funcs: count calls within files of the same package
# - Exclude the declaration file:line itself

# First, let me determine if each function is a method or regular function
grep -rn '^func ' /bench/home/work/internal/ --include='*.go' | \
  grep -v '_test\.go' | \
  perl -ne '
    if (/^([^:]+):(\d+):func\s+\((\w+)\s+\*?(\w+)\)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(/) {
      # method on type $4
      print "$1:$2:$5:method:$4\n";
    } elsif (/^([^:]+):(\d+):func\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(/) {
      print "$1:$2:$3:func:\n";
    }
  ' > /tmp/funcs_typed.txt

# Add package name
while IFS=: read -r filepath lineno funcname functype typename; do
    pkgname=$(grep -m1 '^package ' "$filepath" | awk '{print $2}')
    echo "$filepath:$lineno:$funcname:$functype:$typename:$pkgname"
done < /tmp/funcs_typed.txt > /tmp/funcs_full.txt

wc -l /tmp/funcs_full.txt

#!/bin/bash
# For each function in funcs_full.txt, count fan-in across the entire repo
# Format: filepath:lineno:funcname:functype:typename:pkgname

while IFS=: read -r filepath lineno funcname functype typename pkgname; do
  # Skip init functions
  [[ "$funcname" == "init" ]] && continue
  # Skip test/benchmark/example functions
  [[ "$funcname" =~ ^(Test|Benchmark|Example) ]] && continue
  
  firstchar="${funcname:0:1}"
  
  if [[ "$firstchar" =~ [A-Z] ]]; then
    # Exported function/method
    if [[ "$functype" == "method" ]]; then
      # Method: search for .FuncName( pattern across entire codebase
      # Exclude the declaration line
      count=$(grep -rn "\.${funcname}(" /bench/home/work/ --include='*.go' 2>/dev/null | \
        grep -v "^${filepath}:${lineno}:" | wc -l)
    else
      # Regular exported function: search for pkgname.FuncName pattern
      count=$(grep -rn "${pkgname}\.${funcname}" /bench/home/work/ --include='*.go' 2>/dev/null | \
        grep -v "^${filepath}:${lineno}:" | wc -l)
      
      # Also count calls from within the same package (no package prefix needed)
      pkgdir=$(dirname "$filepath")
      inpkg=$(grep -rn "\b${funcname}\b" "$pkgdir"/ --include='*.go' 2>/dev/null | \
        grep -v "^${filepath}:${lineno}:" | \
        grep -v "^[^:]*:[0-9]*:func " | wc -l)
      count=$((count + inpkg))
    fi
  else
    # Unexported function: can only be called within the same package
    pkgdir=$(dirname "$filepath")
    count=$(grep -rn "\b${funcname}\b(" "$pkgdir"/ --include='*.go' 2>/dev/null | \
      grep -v "^${filepath}:${lineno}:" | wc -l)
  fi
  
  echo "$count:$filepath:$lineno:$funcname:$functype:$typename:$pkgname"
done < /tmp/funcs_full.txt | sort -t: -k1 -rn
SCRIPT

- The `internal/filter/` package dominates the list, with 6 of the top 10 entries. This package implements a filter/query compilation engine.
